correctness.rationale: Fresh reconstruction confirms the theorem. On one parity b_k=a_{epsilon+2k} satisfies Delta^2 b_k=(2/pi)q. Twice summation gives b_k=b_0+k(b_1-b_0)+(2/pi)sum_{j<k}(k-j)q_j. If q_j=L+o(1), the weighted error is o(k^2), hence b_k=(L/pi)k^2+o(k^2) and a_n/n^2->L/(4pi). Conversely b_k=(L/pi)k^2+(-1)^k k^(3/2) has the required normalized quadratic limit but unbounded second differences. An independent numerical regression recovered constant q=7.25 for a quadratic test; finite numerics are not the proof. The final repaired VERIFICATION.md only restores malformed TeX escapes and does not alter the mathematics.
